fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly, as it is the only way in and out for emergency vehicles.
• Keep a clear turnaround area within the property so fire and emergency vehicles can turn around without backing out onto the road.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation that has grown close to the main residence to keep a clear path around the exterior walls.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and move around it.
• Keep the walkway from the driveway to the front entry clear of overgrowth so responders can reach the front door on foot.
• Cut back shrubs or trees that block sightlines from the road to the front entry and driveway entrance.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough that emergency vehicles have room to stage without being blocked by parked cars.
• Post the property address visibly at the road and again at the front entry if the driveway is long enough that the house cannot be seen from the street.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and eaves of the structure.
• Thin the tree canopy around the structure so tree crowns are not touching or overlapping each other close to the house.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the walls and foundation of the structure.
• Clear dead leaves, needles, and plant debris from the roof, gutters, and the ground immediately next to the structure.
• Thin shrubs and small trees between the large trees and the structure to create open ground between them.
• Remove low branches from large trees near the structure up to a height of at least 10 feet from the ground.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along its full length.
• Remove any dead or fallen wood piled near or leaning against the structure.
• Keep the area directly surrounding the structure clear of dry grass, leaves, and loose plant material.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the road.
• Maintain the full width of the access route so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
